items.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017
items.q: We did a couple of Broadway show things and a lot of things for Ray which was fun. I played in those you know.

ctx.x: And I did quite a few of those things. We did a couple of Broadway show things and a lot of things for Ray which was fun. I played in those you know. But over the period of years, when Disney stopped doing all their mega-musical things, it’s too bad. I mean Walt’s idea was a lot of live music but I think, and this is very basic, I think Disney discovered that since the entire continent of South America is going to empty on Orlando every year, they’ve got people coming from Brazil and Argentina. I mean you’ve got…

they didn’t need all this entertainment. And it’s too bad. And I saw it from a business perspective. I saw it happening because when Disney opened, this was October 1, 1971, they had an autonomous entertainment division, with a vice president, you know, a board, I mean boy we could do anything and get anything. And I saw over a period of about two years the entertainment division completely absorbed by operations. It just disappeared.
